articles.headline: Giants' Harbaugh explains reasoning for releasing Beckham
articles.description: Giants coach John Harbaugh on Wednesday explained the team's decision for releasing wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr.
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- Round two just didn't work out for Odell Beckham Jr with the New York Giants. After no catches and just 19 snaps in three games, coach John Harbaugh thought releasing the veteran receiver was the best move for the team and his offense.

Beckham, in his second stint with the team, was released Tuesday. Harbaugh explained the decision on Wednesday.

"Had a great conversation with Odell and it's tough," he said. "But we just weren't getting enough. It just wasn't working for us. And like I told him, I wanted to be able to get more. I wanted him to be able to do more. I wanted to get him on the field more.

"Whatever reason, we weren't able to do it. Put it on us. We weren't able to get it done. At this point in time, that's kind of where we were and we needed to move on."

The Giants are now moving forward with wide receivers Braxton Berrios and Charlie Jones having been added to the active roster this week. New York wanted more out of the roster spot occupied by a fourth wide receiver who offered no special teams value.

Beckham, 33, worked his way onto the roster with a strong summer. He needed it because it was made clear when he signed in the spring that there wasn't a roster spot guaranteed. The season apparently wasn't guaranteed either.

The veteran receiver now is a free agent.

"I hope he lands somewhere. I mean, he's a great friend," Harbaugh said. "I love the guy and I hope he lands somewhere and gets a shot. I think he's determined to, and it'd probably be a better situation for him. It just wasn't working here. And that's really all that needs to be said."

Beckham wasn't the normal bottom-of-the-roster wide receiver. He was drafted by the Giants in the first round of the 2014 NFL draft and began his career with three straight seasons of at least 1,300 yards receiving. He was a fan favorite, a favorite of the grandkids of the owners.

Giants fans were chanting, "OBJ! OBJ! OBJ!" in the fourth quarter of Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans. They wanted something, anything, from the former Pro Bowl receiver.

But Harbaugh insists the attention that Beckham drew by his mere presence didn't have anything do with the move.

"It's what's best for the team. That's it," he said. "And if you think it's anything else, then you don't know me and you don't know what we're doing here. ... I'm not hiding anything. It's not Watergate."

Beckham's not the only change for the Giants offense since the start of the year. They also lost quarterback Jaxson Dart for at least the remainder of the regular season because of a knee injury.

Dart underwent surgery Friday to repair the meniscus and MCL in his left knee.

"The docs said it went well," Harbaugh said. "It was as expected. They saw what they thought they would see and just fixed it. Timeline doesn't really change too much."

articles.headline: What's level of concern for Panthers' notable injuries before Week 4 vs. Lions?
articles.description: Ahead of its first primetime game of the season Sunday, Carolina has seven noteworthy injuries to monitor.
articles.headlineJa: 第4週のライオンズ戦を前に、パンサーズの主な負傷者に対する懸念の度は？
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日に今季初のプライムタイムでの試合を控えるカロライナ（パンサーズ）には、経過を注視すべき主な負傷者が7人いる。
articles.body:
The Carolina Panthers (1-2) will be without their top two cornerbacks for the foreseeable future, and even with two-time Pro Bowl defender Jaycee Horn (quad) and fellow starter Mike Jackson (groin) on injured reserve, the team is monitoring injuries for seven other notable players ahead of Week 4's primetime matchup against the Detroit Lions on "Sunday Night Football." (8:20 ET, NBC).

"No one can replace Jaycee Horn," Panthers coach Dave Canales said Monday. The task for the team's other cornerbacks is to "do their jobs" in relief. But with Jackson also on the injury list, the Panthers' secondary will be tested against the Lions and beyond.

Cornerback is not the only position group facing a challenge with injuries piling up for the Panthers.

Following Carolina's 21-18 Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns, the Panthers are overseeing the injury statuses for several players, including starting quarterback Bryce Young and No. 1 wide receiver Jalen Coker. The MASH unit formed within the Carolina locker room has created issues as the Panthers try to finish the first quarter of the season with a .500 (or better) record for the first time since 2021.

"It's a challenge because you want to know what your [game-day roster] is going to look like on Sunday so that you can have a significant game plan for your guys," Canales said Monday. "At a minimum, we start with the opponent and we say, 'Structurally, these are the things we do well -- how we want to attack.' ... So, we have to be able to look at all of those things and make assumptions based on the information that we have today and tomorrow to get that game plan going. But it presents its challenges."

While the Panthers could see a potential upswing in reinforcements following their Week 5 bye, they still need to contend with a formidable 2-1 Lions squad first.

Here's a look at seven of the Panthers' most notable injuries as of Wednesday's injury report, listed in order of significance to the team:

Bryce Young, QB

Injury: Knee
Wednesday's walk-through status: Full

What happened: Young limped off the field after he was sacked by Browns DT Mason Graham in the second quarter of the Week 3 loss at Cleveland. He returned on the next drive but went to the blue tent during the third quarter before making another immediate comeback. Following the game, Canales said Young was dealing with "something," but the QB said everyone is dealing with "something" in the NFL.

Level of concern - Minor: Canales said Monday that he expected Young to play against Detroit. However, he also said the QB would undergo testing on his lower-body injury. Young led the offense in practice Wednesday without issue.

Biggest issue for Week 4 (or beyond?): Through three weeks, the Lions have 57 QB pressures, which is tied for second in the league with the Atlanta Falcons, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. articles.headline: 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey: 'I want to be judged by winning'
articles.description: Coming off a career year, Tyrese Maxey said he doesn't want to be judged by how he does individually but by how the 76ers do as a team this year.
articles.headlineJa: 76ersのガード、タイリース・マクセイ：「勝利によって評価されたい」
articles.descriptionJa: キャリアハイのシーズンを終えたタイリース・マクセイは、今年は個人の成績ではなく、76ersがチームとしてどう戦うかで評価されたいと語った。
articles.body:
CAMDEN, N.J. -- Having earned two All-Star nods in the last three seasons and coming off a campaign in which he averaged a career-high 28.3 points per game, Philadelphia 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey is primed for another big year.

But the 25-year-old said Wednesday after the Sixers' second practice of training camp that the only metric he cares about for Philadelphia's highly anticipated upcoming season is team success.

"I'm at the point now where I've showed what I can do talent-wise," Maxey said. "Of course, I'm going to continue to get better, but I want to be judged by winning. If we win, that's what I want to be judged by. That's really my main mindset, my main goal, is finding ways to win."

Maxey was the first of Philly's four major stars -- including Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown and LeBron James -- to speak to reporters since training camp started Tuesday.

Brown sidestepped a query on media day Monday when asked about how the Sixers will determine a pecking order and identify an "alpha" by replying: "Next question."

 

Maxey's answer was in the same spirit, albeit much more elaborate, as he detailed his willingness to adjust to help the team.

"Because I've played so many different roles, I'm capable of doing so many different things," Maxey said. "And I think that's going to be a positive for myself and for this team. I can play on the ball. I can play off the ball. I can play in transition. I can catch and shoot. Play off [of] pin downs. I can play pick-and-roll. ...

"I'm going to play however they need me to play. However Coach [Nick Nurse] wants to play, that's how I'm going to play."

And Maxey is not only leading by example. He is speaking up as the new group gets off the ground.

"My voice carries a little bit and then just the charisma of me smiling and having a good time," Maxey said. "I mean, I'm getting older ... and I just feel like I've been here for a minute. Process [Embiid] has been here, I think what, 13 years? I've been here seven. So, we've been here for a while, kind of know how things go around here and just am trying to keep using my voice and help everybody get familiar and help everybody get comfortable."

Beyond vowing to acquiesce to any role change that is asked of him, Maxey also used his voice to be effusive in his praise of the other stars on the team in his answers Wednesday.

On James: "That's like a big brother to me. He's an old man ... He's a good guy. He's a good guy."

On Embiid: "He looks amazing. He looks happy. ... When you're healthy and you're happy and you're at peace with your life and basketball, that's when you're at your best. He's been great."

On Brown: "JB's like physically a freak of nature. He's just stronger than you. He jumps higher than you. He's faster than you and he's very talented. Those are the things that you see every single day. And I think what's stood out to me so far is his communication and he's willing to pick up the ball defensively, kind of just do whatever coach needs hi

articles.headline: Klopp not preparing for more titles after verdict against Man City
articles.description: Jürgen Klopp said Wednesday he would "wait and see" before commenting on the Premier League's announcement yesterday that Manchester City had been found guilty of 114 charges for breaching financial rules.
articles.headlineJa: クロップ監督、マンCへの有罪判決後もさらなるタイトル獲得の準備はせず
articles.descriptionJa: ユルゲン・クロップ監督は水曜日、マンチェスター・シティが財務ルール違反の114件の違反行為で有罪と認定された昨日のプレミアリーグの発表について、コメントする前に「静観する」と語った。
articles.body:
Jürgen Klopp said Wednesday he would wait to see how things pan out before commenting on the Premier League's announcement yesterday that Manchester City had been found guilty of 114 charges for breaching financial rules.

The charges cover a period between 2009 and 2018, with Klopp's tenure at Liverpool -- which began in 2015 -- overlapping with the time that City were have found to be guilty of breaking Premier League rules.

On the eve of Germany's match against Serbia in the Nations League, though, Klopp seemed content to let his record at Merseyside speak for itself instead of speculating over what might have been.

"I haven't given it much thought, even though I've seen it of course," Klopp said. "Should any sanctions be imposed, I naturally have nothing to do with it anyway, and that's why I'm waiting to see how things pan out. But when you're talking about legal proceedings that have been going on for so long now, I assume there will be an appeal or something like that? That will take ages again of course.

"So I'm a long way from preparing myself for it in any way and I don't have any feelings about it."

City, who won the Premier League three times between 2009 and 2018, have denied all of the charges and are set to lodge an appeal against the verdict.

Of his longtime rival and Man City coach Pep Guardiola, Klopp said:  "I also know what I said about it in the past and how if there's ever a parade, I'll be there. But it doesn't feel like that anymore. My respect for Pep Guardiola and the football played at City during the time we played against each other, in the way they played back then and how they brought football to life on the pitch -- plus what an opponent they proved to be for us at the very highest level -- is far too great for me to be able to say anything now."

Klopp was also tight-lipped on Germany's captain for the Nations League tie -- his third match in charge of the national team. The new Germany coach has a completely new squad to work with after he selected two groups for the four fixtures during this international window.

With regular captain Joshua Kimmich allowed to leave the camp after he featured in a 1-1 draw in the Netherlands and the shock home loss to Greece, Klopp must decide who wears the armband for this clash in Munich.

"The team will be led onto the pitch tomorrow by the player with the most international caps," Klopp said on Wednesday.

Captain question aside, Klopp did hint that Bayern Munich goalkeeper Jonas Urbig would play at his home stadium of Allianz Arena.

"Feel free to ask 'who might be a captaincy option,' but I don't reveal the starting lineup now. You can look them up yourselves," said Klopp. "I can only say that Jonas Urbig won't wear the armband in his first international match."

Urbig took part in a news conference after Klopp and expressed his delight at making his Germany debut.

The other 28 teams in the association joined them Monday, ahead of training camps beginning for most teams.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first media day away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their first impressions?

Sept. 30

Nuggets add Nembhard on two-way deal

Guard Ryan Nembhard has agreed to a two-way contract with the Denver Nuggets, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Nembhard, 23, played 60 games (27 starts) for the Dallas Mavericks in 2025-26 after signing as an undrafted free agent. He was traded to the Atlanta Hawks then to the Charlotte Hornets this offseason before being waived.

Sept. 29

Charania: NBA reviewing finalists' bids for Vegas team

ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the NBA is currently reviewing finalist bids for a new expansion team in Las Vegas. The price range is currently speculated at $12-13 billion with a new arena factored into the cost. 

The three final groups are Nancy Walton Laurie and Bill Laurie; Steve Apostolopoulos and Marc Lasry; Bill Foley and Jerry Colangelo, sources told ESPN.

Will KAT take a pay cut in next Knicks deal?

On "NBA Today," ESPN's Malika Andrews detailed Karl-Anthony Towns' mindset toward contract negotiations with the defending champion New York Knicks.

"Towns, from what I have been told, is willing -- similarly to what Jalen Brunson did [but the] numbers aren't the same -- to take a pay cut," Andrews said. "But the pay cut that the Knicks are asking him to take, he views as unreasonable."

Towns, 30, is eligible to sign a four-year, $276 million extension through June 30.

Joel Embiid was a "full participant all the way through" for the Philadelphia 76ers first practice of training camp, Sixers coach Nick Nurse said Tuesday.

After being named the league MVP in 2023, the 32-year-old center has missed 150 games over the last three seasons because of various injuries.

He also sat out four of the Sixers' 11 playoff games in the spring because of appendicitis, right hip soreness and a right ankle sprain.

articles.body:
Josh Allen remains the man to beat for MVP, according to the odds, as he has extended his lead to +260 after coming into the season as the +600 favorite. But the player entering the MVP conversation in earnest is Brock Purdy, who began the season with 10th-best 18-1 odds and is now just behind Allen at +425.

Another big gainer to start the season has been Trevor Lawrence, who has shortened to 10-1 after being 18-1 the week prior and 22-1 at the start of the campaign. On the flip side, Dak Prescott (20-1) and reigning MVP Matthew Stafford (28-1) have lengthened from 12-1 and 14-1, respectively, since the beginning of the season. Caleb Williams is still one of the largest sportsbook liabilities, but he is 55-1 and remains out with an injury.

Jeremiyah Love is starting to run away in the Offensive Rookie of the Year race, showing +150 to the next-closest competitor, Denzel Boston, at +700. Patrick Mahomes remains the odds-on favorite for Comeback Player of the Year at -270, while he is also prominently in the MVP race at +800.

Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Sept. 30: TNF injury updates, 10 trends to know for Week 4

By Michael F. Florio

Rico Dowdle did not practice to start the week and is out for the Pittsburgh Steelers' "Thursday Night Football" matchup with the Cleveland Browns. Last week with him sidelined, Jaylen Warren handled the bulk of opportunities, playing 90% of the snaps and garnering 17 carries and four targets. He finished with 176 total yards and 20.6 fantasy points (RB8).

Warren has a chance to build off of that, as the Browns have allowed the sixth-most yards on outside runs and have missed tackles at the sixth-highest rate in the NFL. Warren should be started over David Montgomery, Quinshon Judkins, Omarion Hampton, Rhamondre Stevenson and Jadarian Price.

Trends to know for Week 4

Defenses have altered the way they play Drake Maye since last season's playoffs. Teams are rushing four men -- or fewer at times -- at a high rate against the New England Patriots, but have still been able to create quick pressure. Last week, the Jacksonville Jaguars rushed four or less on 82% of dropbacks and still created pressure, on average, in under 2.5 seconds. Each team has played Cover-6 at least 15% of the time against Maye.

Simply put, teams are able to get to Maye quickly without blitzing, meaning they are able to drop more players into coverage. Maye has to make quick decisions, and it is not allowing enough time for his receivers to consistently get open. It has also seemingly sped the clock up in his head.

I think Maye will eventually figure it out, and his value will likely never be lower -- especially in dynasty leagues. These struggles create a trade-for opportunity. However, until we see him figure it out, it is very tough to trust him in redraft leagues.

Bryce Young faces a Detroit Lions defense that has allowed the most passing yards and second-most touchdowns to QBs. Every QB to face them has scored at least 23 fantasy points, and they've finished QB8, QB1 and QB3.

Bhayshul Tuten has forced 15 missed tackles on outside runs (second most) and the Cincinnati Bengals have the sixth-highest rate of missed tackles on such runs (40%).

Bucky Irving, who has the fourth-most rushing yards on outside runs, faces the Green Bay Packers, who have allowed the most yards on those runs.

Rashee Rice had eight of his nine targets come against zone defense last week. The Las Vegas Raiders play zone 81% of the time.

articles.headline: Steelers rule Joey Porter out again; Jalen Ramsey questionable
articles.description: Steelers cornerback Joey Porter will miss his fourth straight game as he has officially been declared out for Thursday night's game against the Browns.
articles.headlineJa: スティーラーズ、ジョーイ・ポーターを再び欠場と決定；ジェイレン・ラムジーは出場疑い
articles.descriptionJa: スティーラーズのコーナーバック、ジョーイ・ポーターは木曜夜のブラウンズ戦で正式に欠場と発表され、4試合連続で欠場することになった。
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH -- Despite full participation in back-to-back walk-throughs earlier this week, Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. will not make his season debut against the Cleveland Browns on Thursday night.

Porter was ruled out by the Steelers on Wednesday afternoon, while fellow defensive back Jalen Ramsey (broken wrist) was listed as questionable. The Steelers also ruled out running back Rico Dowdle (toe). And while the Steelers announced cornerback Brandin Echols cleared concussion protocol, he remains listed as questionable.

That Porter, who was inactive for the first three games of the season, was ruled out for Thursday's game is a surprise after being a full practice participant earlier in the week. He seemingly reported a back issue to the Steelers on Wednesday, and the team added "back" alongside the previous injury description of "not injury related/conditioning" on Wednesday's practice report. Porter was also listed as a limited participant.

Just a day earlier, coach Mike McCarthy expressed optimism about Porter's availability for Thursday night's game.

"Oh, we hope so," McCarthy said Tuesday when asked if he expected him to play against the Browns following his full participation Monday. "Today is another day. ... this will be more of a jog-through. We'll have a little more pace and pretty much a similar amount of reps. We'll see how he does today."

McCarthy was deliberate in slowly ramping up his practices on the short week to optimize his team's recovery from the Week 3 win against the Cincinnati Bengals. Monday's practice was a light walk-through, followed by a slight uptick in speed Tuesday and more tempo Wednesday.

Because Monday's and Tuesday's practices weren't full-speed, the participation report is an estimation, but Porter's status as a full participant in each was still significant. It marked the first time he had been a full participant since he was activated off the physically unable to perform list in late August.

While navigating a contentious contract negotiation that failed to produce an extension by the team's regular-season deadline, Porter has also been dealing with a back injury since first reporting the aggravation during a mobility workout on the first day of training camp. He missed all of training camp and the preseason on the physically unable to perform list. He was activated off the list on roster cutdown day, and he had been a limited participant in every practice before this week. He also left practice early two weeks ago when he reported another flare up of his back injury, but the "back" injury description was gone from the practice report by the following week.

Speaking for the first time since he and the Steelers failed to reach an agreement on a contract extension, Porter said on Sept. 24 that he would "definitely" play this season, and he added that both his conditioning and the lingering back injury had been preventing him from playing in games.

articles.body:
Gilberto Mora is subject to interest from Liverpool, while Real Madrid are hoping they can sign Virgil van Dijk when his Liverpool contract expires at the end of the season. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Liverpool are interested in Club Tijuana and Mexico international midfielder Gilberto Mora, according to Football Insider. The Reds are said to be admirers of the 17-year-old, but there is significant competition emerging in the race for his signature, with Real Madrid, Barcelona, and Paris Saint-Germain also keen. The Liga MX side are expected to part ways with him at the end of the season when they believe his value will be at its highest. Mora impressed at the World Cup in the summer and has made an impressive start to the new campaign with five goals in seven matches.

- Liverpool skipper Virgil van Dijk could join Real Madrid on a free transfer when his contract expires at the end of the 2026-27 season, according to Mundo Deportivo. The 35-year-old central defender has not received an offer of a renewal from Liverpool officials, suggesting that his time at the club could be coming to a natural conclusion. Madrid boss Jose Mourinho, who already has Van Dijk's former teammates Trent Alexander-Arnold and Ibrahima Konaté in his defensive ranks, both also signed at the end of their Liverpool contracts, is interested in adding another center back. However, Madrid are not the only club monitoring the situation, with AC Milan, Galatasaray and Inter Miami also mentioned as potential destinations. Van Dijk joined Liverpool in 2018 and helped transform the club's fortunes, playing his part in the club winning every domestic trophy as well as the UEFA Champions League, UEFA Super Cup and FIFA Club World Cup.

- Real Madrid are monitoring the situation of Manchester City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, TEAMtalk reports. Madrid are assessing the transfer market for a long-term option between the posts, and they see the 27-year-old as a strong candidate to succeed Thibaut Courtois due to his experience in the Champions League. Whether City part ways with Donnarumma could hinge on their punishment after they were found guilty on Tuesday of almost all 115 financial charges brought against them by the Premier League. City have until Friday to appeal.

- Barcelona defender Jules Koundé has been placed on the shortlist of Bayern Munich, Diario Sport reports. The Bundesliga club have kept close tabs on the 27-year-old for some time, and they are lining up an approach for him as a potential future successor to defender Kim Min-jae. Kounde signed a new five-year contract back in August 2025, but having failed to establish himself as a starter in La Liga this season, a switch to the Allianz Arena could become a possibility in the January transfer window.
